notes.title: UPDATE #7 (AND #8): MEET THE BOSSES
notes.content:
Hi all. I know it's been two weeks since the last update, when we were aiming for a weekly update to Steam. There's a good reason for that. This update is really meaty...

[h1]BIG CHANGES[/h1]

[b]BIG BOSSES[/b]

We have added the first iteration of the Level 1 (Factory) bosses. They come hot from the oven, having been finished right today. They lack some polish, balancing and testing, but we think they are reaaaally cool and you will like them. In the coming weeks will correct issues and fix bugs related to them. Also, the music is pending mixing and production, but we hope you like them. For those playing with the music off, we highly recommend playing them at least once with the music on =)

As we said somewhere, there will be two possible bosses per level, each in its own area. These two can be found at the end of the Core and Ruined sections of the factory.

We really hope you have a blast fighting them!

[h1]NOT [b]THAT[/b] BIG CHANGES[/h1]

[b]Power Ups[/b]

In this build we are trying another new feature which, for the time being, is limited to the city area. All around it we've placed pickup boxes which can spawn equipment, as usual, or power ups. These pickups can grant either health (instant heal, regeneration or an extra heart), temporal improvements (speed, strength, defence) or permanent improvements for the run (strength, defence).

Since there are other ways in the game to recover health or even get extra hearts (although noone seems to have discovered how), the health power ups are scarce.

[b]City section decoration[/b]

We've been decorating the city section, so it is richer and more interesting to explore. Together with the addition of pickups, we think it has improved quite a bit. Let's see what you think.

[b]New enemy in sewers[/b]

We had forgotten to add one of the scavenger enemies we had completed. It should spawn now from time to time. We have also another police enemy version pending integration, but it will come in a future update.

[b]New controller management system[/b]

We now allow configuring game pads independently. In the gamepad menu you can select which pad to configure. During gameplay, the last active gamepad should be the one we read input from. This should solve problems with gamepads not being recognized as the primary pad by the game.

Due to material limitations we have not been able to test this feature too much (we only have so many pads lying around), so we'd gladly accept feedback, be it positive (set-ups which did not work before, now do) or negative (set-ups which have been broken). In the coming weeks we'll try to create a small tool to check if your gamepads are compatible with the game, and to help you configure them if they aren't.

[h1]BUGFIXING[/h1]

Since we've been focusing in adding content this past weeks, the list of bugfixes is short. However, we are still investigating the few major bugs we have found (crashes in the factory level when changing rooms, mainly).
[list]
[*] Cannot attack normal and police lifter legs
[*] Guns cannot aim at certain enemies
[*] Health recovery plays no sound in level 2
[*] Scrapping main weapon did not place other primary in there
[*] Crashed ship up pickup lacks door barring access to sewer
[*] Duelist gun reticle visible when picked up
[/list]

As the usual caveat: we are working very hard at keeping these updates coming and there are many things than might not work as intended. Please, let us know in the comments if you find any!

notes.title: Update #6: Flybots and other tweaks
notes.content:
Note: due to technical/personal circumstances this week's Mac build will suffer a slight delay. Please, excuse the inconvenint. We'll upload it in the coming days.

[h1]Main changes[/h1]

This week sees the end of Heartloween. As we said in the previous update, it will become part of the game as collectible equipment.

Regarding more important improvements, we are glad to let you know that the two major bugs the game had should be fixed now:
[list]
[*] Flybots are trapped inside their cages
[*] Lots of bolts being spawned in level 2 rendered the game unplayable
[/list]

We have also rebalanced the City area, so it is a little easier now. By reducing the amount of robots spawned in it, the framerate should degrade less than it used to, making the level should be playable.

This rebalance affects the factory and sewers levels, to a certain degree. Enemy waves should be more cohesive now, spawning groups of similar robots. The prevalence of some enemy weapons has also been reduced (flybot laser), to avoid extremely difficult challenges.

[h1]Fixes and improvements[/h1]

Other changes include:
[list]
[*] Small change in how the pick up menu for body parts looks, and fixed an issue which could make its buttons look faded
[*] It is again possible to run with a secondary (gun or shield) weapon equipped
[*] Reduced the conditions in which enemies will stand passive until attacked. There are still some cases when this happens, but we're working on fixing them too
[*] Improved enemy navigation, making them less prone to getting caught in loops between two points in the map
[*] Dogs and smallbots are now able to overcome small heights in the terrain
[*] Improved navigation in the city COPs precinct area
[*] Added an ending sequence to placeholder city boss room
[*] Input options Single Key Run and Alternative Weapon Selection are now independent
[/list]

[h1]Coming soon[/h1]

The art team has been hard at work getting the bosses for level 1 ready. We will start integrating them soon. Once they're finished, they'll start working on the new equipment parts and level 2 bosses. We'll introduce this content in coming builds as it is ready, but please, be patient.

See you in the coming weeks!

notes.title: Update #5: It's Heartloween!
notes.content:
Hello, everyone.

Since Halloween is here, we decided to participate with a small detail. This week's update brings a new look for Heart, a little less techy, but as lovable as it always was.
In coming updates Heart will recover its usual looks and this Heartloween set will be part of the available equipment. It will of course feature appropriate abilities and power ups.

We hope that will answer the eternal question: can robots be afraid?

[h1]Important changes[/h1]

This build also includes some considerable balance tweaks, which we hope you will welcome:
[list]
[*] Enemies tend to get much closer to Heart. That should make them a little more aggressive than before.
[*] Turrets in level 2 fall much faster. This should stop Heart from running away from police control areas, preventing the issues that caused.
[*] It is no longer possible to evade while jumping. This made some equipment (e.g. Italian Boots) hard to balance, and also changed the game a little too much. We will continue tweaking what can and cannot be cancelled into an evasion in coming builds.
[*] We have changed the way the equipment is spawned, so we can integrate the unlocking system later on. Except in very specific situations (hint: some weapons come on rails), no piece of equipment should ever appear twice in a run. Other than that, this change should be invisible to players.
[/list]

We have also decorated some parts of the city and made the COPS ambush in the sewers easier.

[h1]Known game breaking issues[/h1]

Problems we are aware of, which can impact the game experience:
[list]
[*] Sometimes flybots remain inside their insertion boxes. If this happens in an arena, it will probably be unbeatable.
[*] In level 2, a considerable amount of bolts might appear in certain rooms, severely affecting framerate.
[*] Gamepads fail to be recognized in MacOS systems.
[/list]

We are trying hard to fix these issues. Once we're done with them, we'll make a hotfix release.

[h1]Bugfixes[/h1]

The list of bugfixes is smaller this week. But don't fret. We will get back to bug squashing as soon as some major stuff is implemented.
[list]
[*] Falling into the void in boss room of level 2 (reported by Sleepinggiraffe)
[*] Italian boots jump-evade combo (reported by Captain Vag Disaster)
[*] Linux builds fail if install folder has spaces (reported by Uboa Noticed You)
[*] Some equipment were spawners incorrectly placed
[/list]

notes.title: UPDATE #3: HOTFIX UP
notes.content:
Hi all, 

we just uploaded a hotfix for the second weekly update. It includes several fixes (we'll go over all of them on the weekly update changelog) but most importantly, [b]it includes possible fixes for two standing critical bugs: enemies and players going through walls and ceilingas and levels failing to load (and throwing the player into the void).[/b]

I say possible fixes because these issues do not reproduce anymore in our development computers, but we don't dare calling them fixed, since some of you were still having issues while we weren't.

Specifically, the level loading bug is something we haven't seen in two weeks, but you are still reporting. The collision detection failure we did experience sometimes, although not often, and it's now by all our test completely gone in our development computers.

The reason we feel unsure as whether the bugs are fixed is because these are engine quirks. That is, they don't come from specific mistakes we have done (that's easier to fix) but from hard to catch idiosyncracies of the engine (how collisions are detected and assets loaded) that we have limited control of. We love the engine we are using (Unity) and we wouldn't have been able to make this game without it, but every tool has its issues, and these seem to be the ones we are going to be dealing with.

So please, let us know: Are the level loading bug and the crossing walls/floors bug fixed? If they are not fixed, did you see any noticeably improvement (ie: there are still there but they are way less frequent)? Do you notice any performance gain or loss with these cahnges?

We'll be here, reading what you have to say.

notes.title: UPDATE 2# : NEW CAMERA, OVERWORLD AND BUG FIXING
notes.content:
Hi all,

The second Heart&Slash weekly update should be up anytime now on Steam's servers. It's taken a little bit longer than usual (hours, really) because this week we are attending MadridGamesWeek, a videogame tradeshow in Madrid where we are showing the game to hundreds of people who didn't know about it.

But it's not only showing. By watching so many people played the game over and over, we have identified many new bugs. More of that at the end of the update, but this is actually very good news!

Anyway, back to this update. This is our second Steam update, and there are several new features content and bugfixes I want to talk about. Please note that this update has significant code changes made on the game that might make it less stable than the previous build.

[b]1- NEW CAMERA:[/b]
This is, I feel the most important change in this update. There was a nasty bug (basically a system design mistake carried over from the initial prototype) that made the camera update at 30-40 fps, no matter what the real fps of the game was. The issue came from our code updating logic (things that matter) 40 times a second, but updating visuals (things that don't change the behaviour of the game) as fast as we could. But the camera was tied to the logical updates, not the visual ones at it should.  

This is now solved, and the game now runs crazy smooth when high framerates are attained. I think this looks very good indeed! But the change affected many systems that had also to be changed, and it has probably introduced many new bugs. This is the main reason this build might be less stable than the previous one. And why bugs that before seemed to not be there appear now. So yes, please report everything weird you see, specially related to movable elements (like elevators and lasers) that were also changed to accommodate the new camera.

[b]2- OVERWORLD:[/b]
We have also introduced the overworld of level two (called "city"in the menus). Please note this is NOT EVEN CLOSE to how we figure this section should look and play. On the visual side of things, the city still looks way too sparse for us, with the floors in particular being devoid of detail and decorations. On the gameplay side of things, enemy waves, distribution and progression is not implemented yet, so it feels really chaotic and, honestly, not nearly as good as the rest of the game. However, all rooms are now in game and working, so most of the heavy load is done. But what's left is probably the most important!

We will spend the next week iterating and improving on this section of the level, and hopefully next Friday you'll be able to play something way closer to our vision.

[b]3- BUGFIXES:[/b]
This is the list of bugfixes since last week's build:
[list]
[*]XP Pickups don't go to player automatically (now they do)
[*]Minimap appears over "Scrap part" button
[*]Guns impact particles delay simulation until in camera (now they don't)
[*]Linebackers lose focus (now they don't)
[*]Clockwork hands seem not to reset the effect once a level is finished.
[*]Guns have problems with broken lifter in special area in sewers
[*]Player can get stuck between doors in the COP special areas
[*]Performance - Change CC to LUT table
[*]Rocketbody can get you stuck beneath lift
[*]When levels fail to be created, the player spawns in the void
[*]Morningstar vanishes
[*]Equipment icons not present when reaching level 2
[*]Clockwork lens icons
[*]Hammer special attack
[*]Avoid three room loops when connecting doors
[*]Limited number of nodes evaluated for pathfinding
[*]Colliders pass for level 1
[*]Reduced number of rooms per section in level 1 by 1/3, increased difficulty per room by 2
[*]Adjusted weights of first level lifter and giants to increase their 
occurrence
[*]Arenas and sequences force time scale of 1. Fixes issue with Clockwork arms
[*]Fixed mold room
[/list]

As you can see, it's a fairly comprehensive list that addresses most (but not all) of the bugs this community found. Next week we'll keep working through our outstanding bug list!

[b]ON PERFORMANCE:[/b]
Now, I want to say something about performance. There have been a couple of performance improvements in the last build, but there has also been some changes (the camera being the most important one) that actually might have improved "perceived" performance, while diminishing real one. Overall, you should see the game running 4-5 fps faster than previously, but we are not sure and want your input on this.

Performance issues on the game are twofold. 

The first one is logic performance. Basically the game code. This is right now mostly restricted to pathfinding issues and major bugs. In the first level, there's little performance degradation in small rooms even with 8 enemies on screen, but it becomes slightly noticeable the larger the room. We need to do a LOT of pathfinding optimizations, but we don't want to tackle that yet, since it's a big task. These performance issues (bugs and pathfinding) will improve as the game develops. Basically, if the game drops a LOT of frames when a lot of enemies are on screen, it's probably this issue, and it's probably fixable.

The second performance black hole is rendering. Basically, since we are using Unity's rendering and camera's, we have little control over this, except for optimizing the art assets we use. this is an issue right now, since some rooms in the new overworld are obviously not optimized enough. If you notice framerate drops on certain places, regardless of enemies around, you are probably seeing this problem. [b]Please, make an screenshot[/b]. Knowing when this happens to most people will allow us to schedule and prioritize art optimization.

Also, the optional screen post processing effects we are using are very expensive. Specially ambient occlusion. That requires a hefty graphic card, and you should disable it if your performance suffers. 

The good news is that on optimized areas the game runs on a quite wide range of systems, so we thing eventually we will be able to lower our system requirements. But for the time being we are leaving them as they are right now.

[b]NEXT WEEK:[/b]
As I was saying at the beginning of this long post (I should make them shorter), we have discovered a lot of bugs during MGW. While many are trivial and easy to fix, the sheer number (around 40) along the still unfinished state of the new overworld, has made us rethink our next update. Originally it was going to be a minor iteration on the overworld and the integration of a tutorial (that would have doubled as our first "story"section). 

However, right now we think bugfixing and making the overworld as fun to play as level 1 takes priority, so we are pushing the tutorial back and use next week to update this update into something more solid and (hopefully) fun.

If we manage to fix most of these bugs, we will have a much more solid experience from which to keep building the game.

Let me know what you guys think!

[b]ON PERFORMANCE:[/b]
Now, I want to say something about performance. There have been a couple of performance improvements in the last build, but there has also been some changes (the camera being the most important one) that actually might have improved "perceived" performance, while diminishing real one. Overall, you should see the game running 4-5 fps faster than previously, but we are not sure and want your input on this.

Performance issues on the game are twofold. 

The first one is logic performance. Basically the game code. This is right now mostly restricted to pathfinding issues and major bugs. In the first level, there's little performance degradation in small rooms even with 8 enemies on screen, but it becomes slightly noticeable the larger the room. We need to do a LOT of pathfinding optimizations, but we don't want to tackle that yet, since it's a big task. These performance issues (bugs and pathfinding) will improve as the game develops. Basically, if the game drops a LOT of frames when a lot of enemies are on screen, it's probably this issue, and it's probably fixable.

The second performance black hole is rendering. Basically, since we are using Unity's rendering and camera's, we have little control over this, except for optimizing the art assets we use. this is an issue right now, since some rooms in the new overworld are obviously not optimized enough. If you notice framerate drops on certain places, regardless of enemies around, you are probably seeing this problem. [b]Please, make an screenshot[/b]. Knowing when this happens to most people will allow us to schedule and prioritize art optimization.

Also, the optional screen post processing effects we are using are very expensive. Specially ambient occlusion. That requires a hefty graphic card, and you should disable it if your performance suffers. 

The good news is that on optimized areas the game runs on a quite wide range of systems, so we thing eventually we will be able to lower our system requirements. But for the time being we are leaving them as they are right now.

[b]NEXT WEEK:[/b]
As I was saying at the beginning of this long post (I should make them shorter), we have discovered a lot of bugs during MGW. While many are trivial and easy to fix, the sheer number (around 40) along the still unfinished state of the new overworld, has made us rethink our next update. Originally it was going to be a minor iteration on the overworld and the integration of a tutorial (that would have doubled as our first "story"section). 

However, right now we think bugfixing and making the overworld as fun to play as level 1 takes priority, so we are pushing the tutorial back and use next week to update this update into something more solid and (hopefully) fun.

If we manage to fix most of these bugs, we will have a much more solid experience from which to keep building the game.

Let me know what you guys think!

notes.title: NEW BUILD UP: LINUX, BUGFIXING AND CONTENT
notes.content:
Hi all,

It's been a week since we submitted the game to Valve for approval (although it's been only 5 days since we went public) and we already have the first update for Heart&Slash. 

Today's update focused on:
[list]
[*]Getting some content into the sewers part of the second level (the only one available so far).
[*]Fixing some of the bugs our community has pointed out.
[*]Providing a Linux build (so we can start testing this).
[/list]

Let's go over this one by one:

[h1]LINUX BUILD:[/h1]
This build is very preliminary, since we don't have a dedicated Linux development machine. The test environment we are using currently is a Debian running in an underpowered laptop. The graphics driver is Mesa (software rendering), so graphical fidelity is very, very poor. Thus, we cannot guarantee that things will work properly right now. Please, be patient. We are considering options to improve this situation as quickly as possible.

[h1]BUG FIXING:[/h1]
Bugs that have been fixed with this build:
[list]
[*]Controller support for Mac (you need to have the controller active before you start the game. Moreover, sometimes if there's more than one input device -controller- detected, the game might fail to detect the correct one).
[*]Enemies getting stuck on ledges: this should be fixed now.
[*]When entering the second level, the HUD is updated properly now.
[*]The main character should not get stuck into enemies as often.
[*]The dead screen now gives you the option to start again on level 2.
[/list]
If you were suffering from some of these bugs, please test the new build so we can be sure they are gone forever (or so we can squash them should they prove resilient).

[h1]CONTENT[/h1]
We have integrated the following new content:
[list]
[*]Several new sounds were integrated.
[*]The sewers got some love, with some special rooms able to appear there now.
[/list]
We hope you are happy with some of these fixes. 

[b]But this is not all...[/b]

There has been a lot of other work done in the game this week, but it's not yet ready for release. In fact, MOST work has been done on content and features not on this build. However, we can't commit for a release next week, so [b]this is a tentative list of next week changes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Overhaul of the Camera system. Game should feel MUCH smoother now and not like it's running at 30fps while the fps counter is telling you you have 100+fps. 
[*]First pass at the overworld of the second level. This is a HUGE area taht will need some work after next week release, but that will definitely expand the scope of the game.
[*]Fixes to level generation that will make it less likely for the game to crash then (although there are stillinstances when this will happen).
[/list]

Apart from the extra content we will be releasing then (which is a lot, and bring the game much closer to were we want it variety-wise) the camera system overhaul is HUGE. 

I can't stress this more. 

It really changes how the game feels. I didn't realize how constraining the current sytem was, and now I find it very hard to play the current, choppy version. Even if I didn't realize it was choppy before. This is only of importance to those getting over 45 fps, but if you are one of these users, I would heartly (no pun intended) recommend to wait till next Friday so you can experience the game as it should really be...
